I always laugh when I run across articles that pretend to tell us the true meaning of Christmas. They usually go back to Christianity, and say that all the merry making and present giving and mistle toe and holly and the Yule Log are frivolous late additions that take away from the religious aspect of the holiday.

The truth is, these customs were old in the north of Europe before Jesus was even born. Christmas is a celebration of the winter solstice -- the return of the Sun, when the days begin to get longer instead of shorter. It's a pagan celebration at its root. The Christian aspects were merely grafted onto the top of the existing solstice festival. That's right, it isn't pagan frivolities taking over from serious Christian worship, its Christian rites and beliefs distracting from an ancient pagan celebration of the return of the Sun.

I'm not saying there's anything wrong with celebrating the birth of Jesus on Christmas. The mythology of Jesus fits in very well with the mythology of the return of the Sun. I'm just pointing out that merrymaking isn't some late custom that distracts from the seriousness of Christ's mass, it is the celebration that had been going on for many centuries the day Jesus was born.
